1.1: King David was gettin' up there in age, and no matter how many blankets they put on him, bruh just couldn't stay warm.
1.2: So his people was like, 'Aight, we need to find a young woman—a virgin—who can take care of the king, keep him company, and keep him warm at night.'
1.3: So they searched all over Israel for the right girl and found Abishag, a Shunammite, and brought her to David.
1.4: She was real fine, took care of the king, but there wasn't no funny business—David ain't sleep with her.
1.5: Now Adonijah, one of David's sons (his mama was Haggith), started feelin' himself. He was like, 'Ima be king.' So he got himself chariots, horses, and fifty men to run in front of him like he already royalty.
1.6: Thing is, David ain't never really checked Adonijah—never told him no or called him out. Plus, dude was real good lookin' and was born right after Absalom.
1.7: He linked up with Joab (David's military general) and Abiathar the priest, and they both backed him up.
1.8: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah (David's top warrior), Nathan the prophet, and David's real ones ain't rock with Adonijah like that.
1.9: Adonijah threw a whole party near the stone of Zoheleth by En Rogel—sacrificed sheep, oxen, and cattle. He invited all his brothers (David's sons) and even some of the king's crew.
1.10: BUT—he ain't invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty warriors, or Solomon. He knew what he was doin'.
1.11: Nathan, the prophet, pulled up on Bathsheba (Solomon's mama) like, 'Girl, you heard Adonijah out here actin' like he king? And David don't even know about it?'
1.12: Nathan told her, 'Look, if you tryna save your life and Solomon's, I got a plan.'
1.13: 'Go straight to King David and ask, "Didn't you promise me that Solomon would be king? So why Adonijah out here claimin' the throne?"'
1.14: 'And while you still talkin', Ima slide in right after you and back you up.'
1.15: So Bathsheba went to see the king. David was still in bed, old and weak, with Abishag takin' care of him.
1.16: Bathsheba bowed down to the king, and David was like, 'What you need?'
1.17: She said, 'My lord, you promised me in God's name that Solomon would be the next king.'
1.18: 'But now, look! Adonijah crowned himself king, and you don't even know it!'
1.19: 'He threw a huge feast, got Joab, Abiathar, and all your sons over there—but he ain't invite Solomon.'
1.20: 'Everybody in Israel lookin' at you, king. You gotta let them know who's really supposed to take the throne.'
1.21: 'If you don't, when you die, me and Solomon gonna be treated like nobodies—or worse.'
1.22: While Bathsheba was still talkin', Nathan the prophet came in.
1.23: Somebody announced, 'Nathan's here!' and he came in, bowed low before the king.
1.24: Nathan was like, 'My king, did you really say Adonijah should be the next king?'
1.25: 'Cuz he out here throwin' a whole coronation party—sacrificing animals, bringin' all the royal sons and officials, and they all yellin', "Long live King Adonijah!"'
1.26: 'But funny thing is… he ain't invite me, Zadok, Benaiah, or Solomon.'
1.27: 'Did you approve this, my king? Or is this some backdoor power move? Cuz nobody told us.'
1.28: Then King David told his people, 'Bring Bathsheba back in here.'
1.29: David took an oath and said, 'As the Lord lives, who brought me through all my troubles—'
1.30: 'I swear Solomon will be king just like I promised—and it's happening TODAY.'
1.31: Bathsheba bowed and said, 'May my king David live forever!'
1.32: David called for Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah and they pulled up.
1.33: David said, 'Y'all take my officials, put Solomon on my royal mule, and ride down to Gihon.'
1.34: 'There, Zadok & Nathan gon' anoint him king. Then blow the horn and shout, "Long live King Solomon!"'
1.35: 'Then bring him back here. He will sit on my throne and rule in my place. This is official!'
1.36: Benaiah was like, 'Amen! And may God make Solomon's throne even greater than yours, my king.'
1.37: Just like the Lord been with my king, may He be with Solomon too, and make his throne even greater than King David's.
1.38: Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's royal guards put Solomon on David's mule and rode to Gihon.
1.39: Zadok took the oil from the temple and anointed Solomon as king. Then they blew the horn, and the people shouted, 'LONG LIVE KING SOLOMON!'
1.40: The whole city was lit. People playin' flutes, rejoicing—the ground was shaking from all the noise!
1.41: Adonijah and his squad heard the noise while they were eatin'—and Joab was like, 'Uh… why the city sound like it's turnin' up?'
1.42: Then Jonathan (Abiathar's son) pulled up, and Adonijah was like, 'Ayy, you got good news, right?'
1.43: Jonathan said, 'Nope. King David just made Solomon king.'
1.44: 'He sent Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and the royal guards with him. They put him on the king's mule, took him to Gihon, and anointed him king.'
1.45: 'Now Solomon sittin' on the throne and everybody celebratin'—that's the noise y'all heard.'
1.46: 'Even David's people went to bless him, sayin' "May God make Solomon's throne greater than David's!" And David bowed in thanks.'
1.47: 'David literally said, "Blessed be the Lord who let me see my son on the throne before I die!"'
1.48: The king also said, 'Praise the Lord, the God of Israel, for He done put someone on my throne today, and I'm still here to see it!'
1.49: When Adonijah's guests heard that, they scattered like roaches when the lights come on.
1.50: Adonijah ran straight to the altar and grabbed the horns, beggin' for mercy.
1.51: They told Solomon, 'Adonijah scared, holdin' the altar, askin' you not to kill him.'
1.52: Solomon said, 'If he proves he's cool, he's safe. But if he try somethin' funny, he's dead.'
1.53: So they brought Adonijah to Solomon, he bowed low, and Solomon said, "Go home."

2.1: David knew his time was almost up, so he called Solomon in for a real talk.
2.2: Son, everybody gotta go one day. I'm headin' that way now. But listen—be strong, step up, and be a real man.
2.3: Follow The Most High. Do what He says. Keep His commandments, His laws, everything written down in Moses' book. If you do that, you gon' prosper wherever you go.
2.4: God made me a promise—if my sons stay true, walk with Him with all they got, there'll always be one of us sittin' on this throne.
2.5: Now, you already know how Joab did me dirty. He killed two of Israel's top commanders—Abner & Amasa—in peacetime, like we was still at war. Dude got blood all over him.
2.6: You wise, son. Handle him. Don't let him grow old in peace.
2.7: But Barzillai's sons? Show them love. Let them eat at your table, 'cause they was solid when I was runnin' from Absalom.
2.8: Now about Shimei—you know, the dude who cursed me out when I was down bad? Yeah, I spared him, but that don't mean you gotta. You smart—you know what to do. Make sure he don't die peacefully.
2.9: Now don't let him slide, 'cause you smart, and you know what needs to be done. Make sure he don't go to his grave in peace—handle that.
2.10: David passed away and was buried in the City of David.
2.11: He ruled 40 years—7 in Hebron, 33 in Jerusalem.
2.12: And now Solomon was officially king, and the throne was locked in.
2.13: Adonijah (the dude who tried to take the throne) pulled up on Bathsheba, Solomon's mama.
2.14: She was like, 'You coming in peace?' and he said, 'Yeah, yeah, I got something to ask you.'
2.15: You know, the kingdom was supposed to be mine. Everybody thought I'd be king. But now it's Solomon's—'cause God gave it to him.
2.16: So now, I just got one little request. Don't say no to me.
2.17: Can you ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag the Shunammite?
2.18: Bathsheba was like, 'Aight, I'll ask him.'
2.19: She went to Solomon, and Solomon stood up, bowed to his mama, then had a seat brought for her next to him.
2.20: She said, 'I got a small favor to ask. Don't say no.'
2.22: Solomon snapped. "Oh, so now you asking for the whole kingdom too? Why don't you give him my throne while you at it?! Him, Joab, and Abiathar the priest—all of 'em on the same team!"
2.23: Then Solomon made an oath, 'If Adonijah don't die for this, may God strike me down!'
2.24: As surely as God made me king, Adonijah gon' be dead TODAY.
2.25: So Solomon sent Benaiah, and just like that—Adonijah was gone.
2.26: Solomon told Abiathar the priest, 'Go home to Anathoth. You should be dead, but I won't kill you now since you carried the Ark of God for my father.'
2.27: Abiathar got removed as priest, fulfilling the prophecy against Eli's family.
2.28: When Joab heard what happened, he ran straight to the altar and grabbed the horns, hoping to get mercy.
2.29: Solomon was told, 'Joab's at the altar, holdin' on for dear life.'
2.30: Benaiah went to him and said, 'King said come out.' Joab: "Nah, I'll die right here."
2.31: Solomon was like, 'Then let him die there. Handle him. That way, I won't be responsible for all the innocent blood Joab spilled.'
2.32: God gon' repay him for killin' two good men—Abner & Amasa—for no reason.
2.33: Let their blood fall on Joab, but may peace be on David's family forever.
2.34: So Benaiah took Joab out right there. Buried him in the wilderness.
2.35: Solomon put Benaiah over the army and Zadok as priest—Joab and Abiathar were officially replaced.
2.36: Solomon called for Shimei and told him, 'Build a house in Jerusalem, stay there, and don't leave. If you cross the Kidron Brook, you dead.'
2.37: Shimei agreed: 'Sounds good, king.' And he stayed put for a while.
2.38: For three years, everything was cool.
2.39: But then two of Shimei's servants ran away to Gath. He went after them and brought them back.
2.40: So Shimei got up, saddled his donkey, and rode out to Achish in Gath to go get his slaves. He found them and brought them back home.
2.41: When Solomon heard about it, he called Shimei in.
2.42: Didn't I make you swear not to leave? Didn't I say you'd die if you did?
2.44: You know deep down all the dirt you did to my father. Now God is paying you back.
2.45: Meanwhile, I'ma be blessed, and David's throne gon' stay strong forever.
2.46: Then Solomon sent Benaiah, and Shimei was done. The kingdom was now fully established.

3.1: Solomon made a peace deal with Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and married his daughter. He brought her to Jerusalem until he finished buildin' his own palace, God's temple, and the wall around the city.
3.2: Back then, people were still sacrificin' at the high places, 'cause there wasn't a temple built for The Most High yet.
3.3: Solomon loved God and followed the ways of his father David. Only problem? He was still burnin' incense and sacrificin' at the high places.
3.4: One day, Solomon went up to Gibeon, the most important high place, and sacrificed 1,000 burnt offerings on the altar. (Yeah, a THOUSAND. Dude went BIG.)
3.5: That night, God pulled up in Solomon's dream and said: 'Ask me for whatever you want.'
3.6: Solomon said, 'Lord, you always had mercy on my father David, 'cause he was loyal and real with You. And You kept Your promise by puttin' his son (me) on the throne.'
3.7: But Lord, I'm just a kid. I don't know what I'm doin'. You made me king, but this job big!
3.8: Your people are countless, too many to number.
3.9: So what I really need? Give me a wise heart to judge right from wrong. Who else could handle a job this big?
3.10: God was feelin' Solomon's request. He was like, 'Aight, bet.'
3.11: God said, 'Since you asked for wisdom instead of money, long life, or the death of your enemies…'
3.12: 'I got you. You gon' be the wisest king to ever do it—nobody before or after will have wisdom like you.'
3.13: 'But hold up, I'ma also give you what you ain't ask for—riches and honor. Ain't nobody gon' compare to you in your lifetime!'
3.14: 'And if you follow me like David did? I'ma bless you with long life too.'
3.15: Solomon woke up like, 'Yo… was that real?!' Then he went to Jerusalem, sacrificed to God, made peace offerings, and threw a huge feast for his crew.
3.16: One day, two women (who were prostitutes) came to King Solomon to settle a case.
3.17: The first woman said, 'My king, me and this woman live in the same house. I had a baby while she was there.'
3.18: 'Three days later, she had a baby too. We were alone—no witnesses, just us.'
3.19: 'Then one night, her baby died 'cause she accidentally rolled over on him.'
3.20: 'So while I was sleepin', she got up, switched our babies, and left her dead baby next to me.'
3.21: 'When I woke up to feed my baby, I saw he was dead. But when I looked close, I realized—THIS AIN'T MY BABY!'
3.22: Then the second woman snapped back, 'Nah! The live baby is mine, yours is the dead one!' The first woman: 'No, the dead one is yours! Mine is alive!' And they kept goin' back and forth in front of the king.
3.23: Solomon sat back like, 'So y'all both say the baby is yours, huh?'
3.25: He told his men, 'Cut the baby in half and give each woman a piece.'
3.26: The real mother panicked and cried out, 'NO! Give her the baby! Don't kill him!' But the other woman? 'Go ahead, cut him in half—neither of us will have him then.'
3.27: Solomon was like, 'Aight, give the baby to the first woman. SHE the real mama.'
3.28: Word got out FAST. Everybody in Israel heard about the king's decision. They were shook 'cause they saw that God gave Solomon next-level wisdom to bring real justice.

4.1: Solomon was runnin' the whole kingdom of Israel. Dude was in charge of everything.
4.2: Here's his top officials: Azariah, son of Zadok, was the priest.
4.3: Elihoreph & Ahijah (Shisha's sons) were the scribes, and Jehoshaphat (Ahilud's son) was the royal historian.
4.4: Benaiah (Jehoiada's son) was over the army. Zadok & Abiathar were the priests.
4.5: Azariah (Nathan's son) was in charge of the governors. Zabud (Nathan's son) was a priest & Solomon's right-hand man.
4.6: Ahishar ran the palace. Adoniram (Abda's son) handled the labor force.
4.7: Solomon had 12 governors across Israel. Each was responsible for supplying food for the king's household one month a year.
4.8: Ben-Hur was over the mountains of Ephraim.
4.9: Ben-Deker ran Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan.
4.10: Ben-Hesed was in charge of Arubboth, Sochoh, and all of Hepher.
4.11: Ben-Abinadab controlled the regions of Dor. (He was also married to Solomon's daughter, Taphath.)
4.12: Baana (Ahilud's son) ruled Taanach, Megiddo, and Beth Shean, plus everything near Jezreel.
4.13: Ben-Geber ran Ramoth-Gilead. He controlled 60 walled cities with bronze gates in Bashan.
4.15: Ahimaaz had Naphtali. (He married Solomon's daughter, Basemath.)
4.16: Baanah (Hushai's son) was over Asher and Aloth.
4.19: Geber (Uri's son) ran Gilead—covering what used to be the lands of King Sihon (Amorites) & King Og (Bashan). (He was the only governor in that region.)
4.20: Judah & Israel was THRIVIN'—as many people as the sand on the shore. Everybody eatin', drinkin', and livin' good.
4.21: Solomon ruled over everything from the Euphrates to Egypt. All the nations in his territory paid tribute and stayed loyal.
4.22: Dude's daily grocery list? 30 kors of fine flour, 60 kors of meal, 10 fat oxen, 20 pasture oxen, and 100 sheep, plus deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened birds.
4.23: Every single day, Solomon's kitchen was STACKED—he had 10 fattened oxen, 20 pasture-fed oxen, 100 sheep, plus deer, gazelles, roebucks, and specially fattened birds.
4.24: He ruled everything from Tiphsah to Gaza. All the kings under him stayed in check, and there was peace all around.
4.25: Judah & Israel lived safely, from Dan to Beersheba. Everybody chillin' under their own fig tree & vine—no worries, no drama.
4.26: Solomon had 40,000 stalls for his chariot horses & 12,000 horsemen.
4.27: Each governor made sure Solomon's table was fully stocked during their month—never ran out of anything.
4.28: They also made sure the horses had what they needed—barley & straw, delivered right on time.
4.29: God gave Solomon crazy wisdom, deep understanding, and a big heart—like the sand on the shore.
4.30: He was smarter than ALL the wise men of the East & Egypt.
4.31: He outshined Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Chalcol, and Darda. His reputation spread EVERYWHERE.
4.32: Dude wrote 3,000 proverbs & 1,005 songs. (Yeah, he had bars. 🎤🔥)
4.33: He knew about everything—trees, plants, animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
4.34: People from ALL nations came to hear him speak—kings sent folks just to soak up his knowledge.

5.1: When Hiram, king of Tyre, heard Solomon got anointed as king after David, he sent his people to congratulate him. Hiram had always rocked with David.
5.2: Solomon sent a message back to Hiram, sayin':
5.3: You already know my father David wanted to build a house for the Lord. But he couldn't—he was too busy fightin' wars on all sides.
5.4: But now, God gave me peace all around. No enemies, no drama—just straight-up rest.
5.5: So now, I'm about to build that house for the Lord, just like He told my father. He said, 'Your son will be the one to build it.' So I'ma make it happen.
5.6: I need you to send me cedar trees from Lebanon. My workers will team up with yours, and I'll pay whatever you ask. 'Cause ain't nobody cut timber like the Sidonians.
5.7: When Hiram heard Solomon's message, he was hype. He said, 'Blessed be the Lord for giving David a wise son to rule over this great people!'
5.8: Hiram sent back a message: 'Bet. I got your request, and I'ma hook you up with all the cedar & cypress logs you need.'
5.9: My workers will cut the wood, send it down to the sea, and float it as rafts to wherever you want. Then you can take it from there. All I ask in return? Feed my people. Give us food for my household, and we're good.
5.10: So Hiram sent Solomon all the cedar & cypress he asked for.
5.11: In exchange, Solomon sent Hiram 20,000 kors of wheat & 20 kors of pressed oil every year. They had a whole food-for-wood trade deal.
5.12: God kept His promise to Solomon, givin' him wisdom. There was peace between Hiram & Solomon, and they made a treaty together.
5.13: Solomon raised a labor force from all Israel—30,000 workers.
5.14: He sent them in shifts: 10,000 at a time—one month workin' in Lebanon, two months back home. Adoniram was in charge of them.
5.15: Besides that, he had 70,000 carriers (the ones haulin' materials) and 80,000 stonecutters (quarrying stone in the mountains).
5.16: And over all of them, there were 3,300 supervisors makin' sure the work got done right.
5.17: Solomon commanded them to cut out massive stones—high-quality, expensive stones—to lay the foundation of the Temple.
5.18: Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the Gebalites all worked together, gettin' the timber and stones ready.

6.1: 480 years after Israel left Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, he started buildin' the Lord's temple. It was the month of Ziv (second month of the year).
6.2: The temple measurements? 60 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, 30 cubits high.
6.3: The front porch was 20 cubits wide (same as the temple) and stuck out 10 cubits.
6.4: Solomon had special windows built with slanted frames.
6.5: Solomon built side rooms all around the outside walls of the temple—surroundin' both the main hall & inner sanctuary.
6.6: The lower rooms were 5 cubits wide, the middle rooms 6 cubits, and the top rooms 7 cubits. He made it so the beams didn't have to be drilled into the temple walls.
6.7: Everything was built from pre-cut stone—so no hammers, chisels, or iron tools were heard inside while it was bein' built.
6.8: The entrance to the middle floor was on the right side of the temple. They used stairs to go up to the second and third floors.
6.9: Solomon built the main temple structure and finished it. He put cedar beams and boards for the roof.
6.10: The side chambers were 5 cubits high and attached to the temple with cedar beams.
6.11: Then God spoke to Solomon, sayin':
6.12: About this temple you buildin'—if you follow My laws, keep My commands, and walk in My ways, I'ma keep My promise to your father David.
6.13: I'ma stay with My people Israel. I won't abandon them.
6.14: So Solomon kept buildin' the temple until it was done.
6.15: Inside, he lined the walls with cedar panels from floor to ceiling. He covered the floors with cypress planks.
6.16: The Most Holy Place (inner sanctuary) was 20 cubits deep, covered completely with cedar boards from floor to ceiling.
6.17: The main sanctuary was 40 cubits long.
6.18: Inside the temple was all cedar—carved with flower buds & blossoms. No stone was visible.
6.19: Inside the temple, he set up the Most Holy Place to hold the Ark of the Covenant.
6.20: The inner sanctuary was a perfect cube—20 cubits wide, long, and high. He covered it in pure gold and built an altar of cedar.
6.21: The whole inside of the temple was overlaid with pure gold.
6.22: He didn't miss a spot—everything in the inner sanctuary was covered in gold, including the entire altar.
6.23: Inside the Most Holy Place, Solomon made two massive cherubim out of olive wood—each one was 10 cubits high.
6.24: Each cherub had two wings—5 cubits long on each side, making them 10 cubits from wingtip to wingtip.
6.25: Both cherubim were identical in size and shape—each one was 10 cubits tall.
6.26: Their wings stretched out—one wing touched one wall, the other wing touched the other wall, and their wings met in the middle.
6.27: He placed the cherubim inside the inner room, stretchin' their wings out wide. One wing touched one wall, the other cherub's wing touched the opposite wall, and in the middle, their wings touched each other.
6.28: And of course, he covered them in gold.
6.29: Solomon carved cherubim, palm trees, and flowers all over the temple walls—inside and out.
6.30: Even the floors were covered in gold—everywhere.
6.31: The inner sanctuary had olive wood doors, set into a five-sided doorframe.
6.32: The two doors were carved with cherubim, palm trees, and flowers. Then they were covered in gold.
6.33: The entrance to the main sanctuary had another set of olive wood doorposts.
6.34: The doors were made of cypress—each one had two folding panels.
6.35: Solomon had cherubim, palm trees, and flowers carved into them too—then covered in gold evenly.
6.36: The inner courtyard was built with three rows of cut stone and a row of cedar beams.
6.37: In the fourth year of Solomon's reign, during the month of Ziv, they laid the foundation of the Lord's temple.
6.38: In the eleventh year, during the month of Bul (eighth month), the temple was finally finished—7 years later, exactly how Solomon planned it.

7.1: Took Solomon 13 years to finish buildin' his palace—yeah, longer than the Temple. But when he was done, it was a masterpiece.
7.2: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon, 100 cubits long, 50 wide, 30 high. It had four rows of cedar pillars and cedar beams across them.
7.3: The roof? Straight-up cedar planks on top of 45 beams, arranged in three rows of 15.
7.4: The windows were in three rows, set directly across from each other.
7.5: All the doorways and posts were squared off, with windows facing each other in three tiers.
7.6: He also built the Hall of Pillars, 50 cubits long, 30 wide—had a front porch with pillars and a canopy.
7.7: Then came the Hall of Judgment—that's where Solomon handled business. He lined it floor to ceiling with cedar.
7.8: His personal house had a courtyard just like this. He even built a special house for Pharaoh's daughter (his wife), styled the same way.
7.9: Every part of these buildings? Made with top-tier stone, cut and polished inside & out—from the foundation all the way to the roof.
7.10: The foundation stones were HUGE—some 10 cubits, some 8 cubits.
7.11: Above that? More perfectly cut stone and cedar wood.
7.12: The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of cut stone and a row of cedar beams—just like the inner court of the Temple.
7.13: Solomon called up Hiram from Tyre, a top-tier metalworker.
7.14: Dude's mama was from Naphtali, his dad was a skilled bronze worker from Tyre. Hiram was gifted—full of wisdom & skill for working with bronze.
7.15: First, he cast two massive bronze pillars, each 18 cubits tall and 12 cubits around.
7.16: He made two bronze capitals (decorative tops) for the pillars, each 5 cubits high.
7.17: He designed them with seven rows of chainwork for decoration.
7.18: He also put two rows of pomegranates around the capitals—same design for both.
7.19: The capitals were shaped like lilies, 4 cubits tall.
7.20: Each capital had 200 pomegranates arranged in rows all the way around.
7.21: When he set them up at the Temple entrance: The right pillar was named Jachin (meaning 'He establishes') The left pillar was called Boaz (meaning 'In Him is strength')
7.22: The tops were shaped like lilies—and just like that, the pillars were done.
7.23: Hiram made a huge bronze basin called 'The Sea'—10 cubits across, 5 cubits high, 30 cubits around.
7.24: It was decorated with ornamental buds all around—10 per cubit, cast as part of the basin.
7.25: It stood on 12 bronze oxen: 3 facing north, 3 facing west, 3 facing south, 3 facing east. The basin rested on their backs, facing outward.
7.26: It was as thick as a handbreadth and had a rim shaped like a cup or lily blossom. It held 2,000 baths of water.
7.27: Hiram made 10 bronze carts (movable wash basins), each 4 cubits long & wide, 3 cubits high.
7.28: Each cart had decorative panels between the frames.
7.29: On the panels, he carved lions, oxen, & cherubim—with braided wreaths underneath.
7.30: Each cart had four bronze wheels with bronze axles, and decorative supports at each corner.
7.31: The top was shaped like a pedestal, 1 cubit across, with engraved decorations. The side panels were square, not round.
7.32: Under the panels were 4 large wheels, with axles attached to the cart. The wheels were 1.5 cubits high.
7.33: These wheels were crafted like chariot wheels, with bronze spokes, rims, and hubs.
7.34: Each cart had four corner supports, made as part of the cart itself.
7.35: At the very top of the cart was a perfectly round piece (half a cubit high), and more decorative flanges & panels.
7.36: He engraved cherubim, lions, & palm trees all over it, adding decorative wreaths.
7.37: All 10 carts were made exactly the same—same design, size, and shape.
7.38: Then he made 10 bronze lavers (basins), each holding 40 baths of water and measuring 4 cubits across.
7.39: He placed 5 carts on the right side of the Temple, 5 on the left. The giant Bronze Sea was set on the right side, near the southeast corner.
7.40: Hiram also made the lavers, shovels, and bowls for the Temple. He finished all the work Solomon hired him for.
7.41: This included: 2 giant bronze pillars, 2 bowl-shaped capitals for the pillars, 2 decorative networks covering the capitals, 400 bronze pomegranates (200 on each network)
7.44: 1 giant Bronze Sea & 12 oxen under it
7.45: He also made bronze pots, shovels, and bowls.
7.46: All this bronze work was cast in clay molds near the Jordan River, between Succoth & Zaretan.
7.47: Solomon didn't even bother weighin' all the bronze—there was too much to count!
7.48: Solomon had all the final Temple pieces made: Gold altar, Gold table for showbread
7.49: 10 pure gold lampstands (5 on each side), plus the gold flowers, lamps, and wick trimmers.
7.50: Everything in the Temple was pure gold—basins, trimmers, bowls, ladles, censers, and even the door hinges!
7.51: Finally, Solomon brought in all the gold, silver, & sacred items David had dedicated and stored them in the Temple treasuries. The work was done.

8.1: Solomon gathered all the elders, tribal leaders, and heads of Israel in Jerusalem. It was time to bring the Ark of the Covenant from the City of David (Zion) to the new temple.
8.2: All the people of Israel pulled up for the Feast of Ethanim (seventh month) to witness this big moment.
8.3: The elders arrived, and the priests carried the Ark.
8.4: They brought up the Ark of the Lord, the Tabernacle, and all the sacred furnishings. The priests and Levites handled it all.
8.5: King Solomon and the entire congregation went all out—they sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that nobody could even keep count.
8.6: The priests brought the Ark into the Most Holy Place, placing it under the wings of the cherubim.
8.7: The cherubim had their wings stretched out, covering the Ark and its poles.
8.8: The poles extended out so you could see their ends from the Holy Place (but not from outside). And they're still there today.
8.9: Inside the Ark? Just the two stone tablets Moses put there at Horeb when the Lord made a covenant with Israel after leading them out of Egypt.
8.10: As soon as the priests left the Holy Place, a cloud filled the Lord's house.
8.11: The cloud was so thick, the priests couldn't even keep ministering—God's presence took over!
8.12: Then Solomon said: 'The Lord said He'd dwell in a dark cloud.'
8.13: I've built You a majestic house—a place for You to stay forever.
8.14: Then he turned around, blessed the crowd, and everyone stood up.
8.15: Solomon spoke: 'Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who spoke to my father David and now made it happen with His own hands.'
8.16: Since I brought My people out of Egypt, I never picked a city for My temple—but I chose David to lead Israel.
8.17: David wanted to build a temple for God.
8.18: But God told him: 'It's good that you want this, but you won't build it—your son will.'
8.19: That's why I'm here—God kept His word. Now I sit on David's throne, and I built this temple in the Lord's name.
8.20: I made a place for the Ark, where God's covenant with Israel is kept.
8.21: Solomon stood in front of God's altar, spread his hands to heaven, and prayed:
8.22: Lord, there ain't nobody like You! No God in heaven or earth who keeps promises like You!
8.23: You kept Your promise to David, my father. You said it, and You did it.
8.24: Now, God of Israel, keep Your next promise: 'David's sons will sit on the throne, as long as they walk in My ways.'
8.25: Lord, please let this promise be fulfilled!
8.26: But for real… will You actually live on earth? Even the highest heavens can't hold You, let alone this temple!
8.27: Still, please hear my prayer, Lord. Listen when I cry out today.
8.28: Let Your eyes always be on this temple, the place where You said, 'My name will be here.'
8.29: When Your people pray toward this temple, please hear them from heaven and forgive them.
8.30: If someone sins and comes here to swear an oath, judge between the guilty and the innocent.
8.31: When Israel loses a battle because of sin, but then they turn back, confess, and pray at this temple, hear them and restore them.
8.32: Then, Lord, up in heaven, hear their case and make the call—punish the guilty for what they did, and clear the righteous, blessin' them for doin' right.
8.33: If Your people Israel take an L in battle 'cause they messed up and sinned against You, but then realize they was wrong, turn back to You, call on Your name, and pray at this temple,
8.34: Lord, when You hear from heaven, forgive Your people's sins and bring them back to their land—the land You promised their ancestors.
8.35: If the sky dries up and there's no rain 'cause we messed up, and we turn back to You, pray, and confess Your name,
8.36: Then Lord, hear from heaven, forgive us, and show us the right way to live. Send rain on the land You gave us!
8.37: If there's a famine, disease, locusts, mildew, or an enemy attack, or any kind of disaster—whatever the crisis may be,
8.38: If anyone in Israel recognizes their struggle and prays toward this temple,
8.39: Lord, hear from heaven and forgive. Answer according to each person's heart, 'cause You alone know what's inside all of us.
8.40: So that Your people will always fear You and follow You while they live in this land You gave us.
8.41: And Lord, when foreigners come here to pray—people who ain't even from Israel,
8.42: Because they heard about Your great name, power, and mighty hand,
8.43: Hear them from heaven and answer their prayers too!
8.44: Let all the nations know who You are and that this temple carries Your name.
8.45: When Israel goes to fight their enemies, wherever You send them, and they pray toward this city and temple,
8.46: Lord, hear them and make sure they win.
8.47: If they sin against You (and let's be real, nobody's perfect), and You let them get captured by their enemies,
8.48: But they come to their senses while in exile and pray to You, saying, 'We messed up, Lord—we did wrong,'
8.49: If they return to You with all their heart and pray toward their homeland and temple,
8.50: Lord, hear them, forgive them, and give them favor with their captors. Let them have mercy on them.
8.51: 'Cause these folks? They belong to You. You brought them out of Egypt, out of the fire, out of slavery.
8.52: Lord, keep Your eyes and ears open to the prayers of Your servant and Your people.
8.53: You made us Your special people, set apart from everyone else—just like You told Moses when You freed us from Egypt.
8.54: When Solomon finished this whole prayer and plea, he got up from kneeling before the altar, hands still lifted to heaven.
8.55: He turned and blessed the whole crowd with a loud voice:
8.56: 'Bless the Lord! He gave rest to His people, just like He promised. Not one word of His promise has failed!'
8.57: 'May the Lord be with us like He was with our ancestors—may He never leave or abandon us.
8.58: May He turn our hearts toward Him, so we can walk in His ways and keep His commandments.'
8.59: 'And may this prayer stay close to God's heart day and night, so He always watches over us.
8.60: 'That way, the whole world will know that the Lord is the one and only God!'
8.61: 'So y'all—stay loyal to God. Walk in His ways, keep His commandments, just like you're doing now.'
8.62: Then Solomon and all of Israel made huge sacrifices before the Lord.
8.63: Solomon offered 22,000 bulls and 120,000 sheep—that's how they dedicated the Temple!
8.64: That same day, Solomon consecrated the middle court in front of the temple. They used it to offer burnt sacrifices, grain offerings, and peace offerings—because the bronze altar wasn't big enough!
8.65: They held a massive feast for 14 days straight—all of Israel, from Hamath to the Brook of Egypt, turned up in worship before the Lord!
8.66: On the eighth day, Solomon sent everybody home. The people left joyful and full of gratitude for everything the Lord had done for David and for Israel!

9.1: When Solomon finished buildin' the Lord's temple, his own palace, and everything else he wanted to do,
9.2: The Lord appeared to him again, just like He did back at Gibeon.
9.3: God said, 'I heard your prayer, Solomon. I've made this house holy, put My name here forever—My eyes and My heart gon' be on it always.'
9.4: 'But listen—if you walk before Me like your daddy David did, with integrity and righteousness, keeping My commandments,
9.5: Then I'll keep My promise. Your kingdom will stay in your family forever.'
9.6: 'But if you or your kids turn away from Me, start chasing other gods, worshiping idols,
9.7: I'm kicking y'all out the land I gave you, and this temple I made holy? I'll throw it away like it's nothing. Israel will be a joke among the nations.
9.8: People gon' pass by and say, "Dang, what happened? Why did God do them like this?"
9.9: And folks will answer, "'Cause they turned their backs on the Lord, started messin' with other gods, and forgot the One who brought them out of Egypt."'
9.10: After 20 years of Solomon building the Lord's temple and his palace,
9.11: King Hiram of Tyre (who hooked Solomon up with all that cedar, cypress, and gold) got a gift back—20 cities in Galilee.
9.12: Hiram went to check out his new cities… and he wasn't feelin' 'em.
9.13: He said, 'Bruh, what kinda cities are these? This the best you got, my brother?' He called them Cabul (which basically means 'good for nothing').
9.14: Still, Hiram sent Solomon 120 talents of gold (that's a lot of money).
9.15: Solomon put together a whole workforce to build the Lord's temple, his own palace, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
9.16: Pharaoh (Solomon's father-in-law) had already conquered Gezer, wiped out the Canaanites there, and gave it as a dowry when Solomon married his daughter.
9.17: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, along with Lower Beth Horon, Baalath, and Tadmor in Judah.
9.18: He also built storage cities, chariot cities, cavalry cities, and whatever else he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and his whole kingdom.
9.19: All the cities Solomon had for storage, plus his chariot cities and cavalry cities, and whatever else he felt like buildin'—whether in Jerusalem, Lebanon, or anywhere else in his kingdom.
9.20: Now, about the folks left in the land—the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the Israelites hadn't wiped 'em all out.
9.21: So Solomon put them to work as forced labor, and that's how it stayed.
9.22: But he didn't make Israelites slaves. They were his warriors, officers, commanders, and leaders.
9.23: His top officials? 550 men in charge of all the work projects.
9.24: Meanwhile, Pharaoh's daughter moved out of the City of David into her new palace Solomon built for her. Then Solomon finished up work on the Millo.
9.25: Three times a year, Solomon offered sacrifices and burnt offerings on the altar he built for the Lord. He also burned incense. The temple was fully up and running.
9.26: Solomon built a whole fleet of ships at Ezion Geber, near Elath on the Red Sea coast (Edom).
9.27: King Hiram sent his best sailors to work with Solomon's crew—'cause these men knew the sea.
9.28: They sailed to Ophir (a place known for mad wealth) and brought back 420 talents of gold to Solomon.

10.1: When the Queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame and wisdom, all tied to the Lord's name, she had to see for herself. So she pulled up to Jerusalem with a whole squad—camels packed with spices, gold, and precious stones—ready to test Solomon with hard questions.
10.2: She came through, sat with Solomon, and asked everything on her mind.
10.3: Solomon had all the answers—there wasn't nothin' too deep or too hard for him to explain.
10.4: When she saw Solomon's wisdom, his palace, the food on his table, how his servants moved, their drip, and even his cupbearers, she was speechless.
10.5: And when she saw how he went up to the Lord's house, she knew she was witnessing something different.
10.6: She told Solomon, "Man, I heard about you in my country, but I ain't believe it till now."
10.7: "They ain't even tell me the half! You way wiser and richer than the stories I heard."
10.8: "Your people are lucky. Your servants are blessed, 'cause they get to be around you and hear your wisdom every day."
10.9: "Blessed be the Lord your God! He was real happy to put you on this throne. 'Cause He loves Israel so much, He made you king to lead with justice and righteousness."
10.10: Then she gave Solomon 120 talents of gold, more spices than anyone had ever brought before, and precious stones.
10.11: Even Hiram's ships brought gold from Ophir, along with a huge shipment of almug wood and more precious stones.
10.12: With that almug wood, Solomon made steps for the temple and his palace, plus harps and stringed instruments for musicians. Nobody had ever seen that much almug wood before.
10.13: King Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba everything she asked for, plus gifts from his royal stash. After that, she and her whole crew went back home.
10.14: Every year, Solomon racked up 666 talents of gold.
10.15: That's not even counting what he got from traders, merchants, Arabian kings, and regional governors.
10.16: Solomon had 200 large shields made outta hammered gold, each one using 600 shekels of gold.
10.17: He also made 300 smaller shields, each one using three minas of gold. He kept them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
10.18: Then he built a huge ivory throne and covered it in pure gold.
10.19: The throne had six steps, a rounded back, armrests on both sides, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
10.20: Twelve lions stood on the steps, one on each side. No other kingdom had a throne like that.
10.21: Everything Solomon drank from was gold. Silver? That wasn't even considered valuable in Solomon's time.
10.22: He had merchant ships sailing with Hiram's fleet, bringing in gold, silver, ivory, apes, and monkeys every three years.
10.23: Solomon was richer and wiser than all the kings on earth.
10.24: Everybody wanted to hear his wisdom, since God had blessed him with so much knowledge.
10.25: So every year, people came through bringing silver, gold, robes, armor, spices, horses, and mules—a steady flow of gifts.
10.26: Solomon stacked up chariots and horsemen—1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen—stationed in chariot cities and in Jerusalem.
10.27: Silver was everywhere in Jerusalem, as common as stones. Cedar wood was as plentiful as sycamore trees in the lowlands.
10.28: Solomon had horses imported from Egypt and Keveh. His merchants bought them at the going rate.
10.29: A chariot from Egypt cost 600 shekels of silver, and a horse cost 150 shekels. They also exported them to the Hittite and Syrian kings.

11.1: King Solomon had a thing for foreign women—Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, Hittites, and even Pharaoh's daughter.
11.2: These were the very nations God told Israel not to mix with, sayin', 'They gon' turn y'all hearts away from Me.' But Solomon? He ain't listen—he was in love.
11.3: Bruh had 700 wives (all princesses) and 300 side chicks—and they pulled his heart away from the Lord.
11.4: When Solomon got old, his wives had him worshiping other gods instead of staying loyal to the Lord like his father David.
11.5: Solomon started messin' with Ashtoreth, the Sidonian goddess, and Milcom, the nasty god of the Ammonites.
11.6: Solomon was out here doin' wrong in God's sight. He wasn't ridin' for the Lord like his pops David did.
11.7: He straight up built altars for Chemosh (the Moabite idol) and Molech (the terrible god of the Ammonites)—right outside Jerusalem!
11.8: Not just that—he did the same for all his wives so they could burn incense and sacrifice to their gods.
11.9: The Lord was big mad at Solomon, 'cause Solomon turned his heart away—even after God had appeared to him twice!
11.10: God straight up told Solomon not to chase after other gods, but he did it anyway.
11.11: So the Lord said, 'Since you broke My commands and ain't listen, I'ma snatch the kingdom from you and hand it to one of your own servants.'
11.12: But outta respect for David, I won't do it while you alive—I'ma take it from your son.
11.13: Even then, I won't take everything—your son will keep one tribe for David's sake, and for Jerusalem, My chosen city.
11.14: God raised up an enemy against Solomon—Hadad the Edomite, a royal descendant from Edom.
11.15: Back when David was wipin' out Edom, Joab (David's army commander) had killed every male in the land.
11.16: Joab stayed there six months straight, makin' sure no males were left in Edom.
11.17: Hadad, just a young boy at the time, dipped to Egypt with some of his father's servants.
11.18: They traveled through Midian and Paran, then took some men with 'em and went to Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
11.19: Hadad became tight with Pharaoh, so much so that Pharaoh gave him his wife's sister (Queen Tahpenes' sister) as his wife.
11.20: They had a son, Genubath, who was raised right in Pharaoh's palace alongside the royal kids.
11.21: But when Hadad heard David and Joab were dead, he told Pharaoh, 'Let me go back home.'
11.22: Pharaoh was like, 'Why? Ain't you got everything you need here?' But Hadad was set—he just wanted to go.
11.23: Then God raised up another enemy—Rezon, son of Eliadah. This dude had fled from his king, Hadadezer of Zobah.
11.24: Rezon gathered men and became a gang leader after David had defeated Zobah.
11.25: He went and took over Damascus, set up shop, and stayed beefin' with Israel all Solomon's days.
11.26: Then came Jeroboam, Solomon's servant—a strong dude from the tribe of Ephraim. His mama was a widow named Zeruah.
11.27: This is how he started rebelling: Solomon was rebuilding the Millo and fixing the City of David.
11.28: Jeroboam was a natural leader—Solomon saw his work ethic and put him in charge of the whole labor force from the tribe of Joseph.
11.29: One day, Jeroboam was leavin' Jerusalem when Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh met him in a field.
11.30: Ahijah had a new cloak on—he straight up tore it into twelve pieces.
11.31: Then he told Jeroboam, 'Take ten pieces—'cause the Lord says, "I'ma snatch ten tribes from Solomon's kingdom and give 'em to you."
11.32: Solomon's son will keep one tribe 'cause of David and Jerusalem, My chosen city.
11.33: All this happening 'cause Solomon and the people turned away from Me, worshiping Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom, instead of following My ways.
11.34: But I ain't gon' take everything from Solomon—I'ma let him rule all his life outta respect for David, My servant.
11.35: But after him, I'ma take the kingdom from his son and give you ten tribes.
11.36: His son will keep one tribe so that David's family always has a presence in Jerusalem.
11.37: Jeroboam, I'ma make you king over whatever your heart desires.
11.38: If you follow My ways, keep My commands like David did, I'ma be with you and build you a lasting kingdom like I did for David.
11.39: I'ma humble David's descendants for this, but not forever.'
11.40: Solomon caught wind of Jeroboam's rebellion and tried to kill him. But Jeroboam ran to Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died.
11.41: The rest of Solomon's story, all his accomplishments and wisdom? They written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon.
11.42: He reigned in Jerusalem for forty years over all Israel.
11.43: Then Solomon died, was buried in the City of David, and his son Rehoboam took the throne.

12.1: Rehoboam rolled up to Shechem, 'cause all Israel was gatherin' there to crown him king.
12.2: Meanwhile, Jeroboam (who was still in Egypt 'cause he ran from Solomon) heard about all this.
12.3: The people sent for Jeroboam. When he got there, him and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam with a request.
12.4: They said, 'Look, your daddy worked us to the bone. If you ease up on these harsh labor laws, we'll gladly serve you.'
12.5: Rehoboam was like, 'Give me three days to think about it.' So the people bounced.
12.6: First, Rehoboam asked the old heads (Solomon's advisors) what he should do.
12.7: They told him, 'If you ease up and treat them right, they'll be loyal forever.'
12.8: But Rehoboam wasn't feelin' that. Instead, he asked his homeboys—the ones he grew up with.
12.9: He said, 'What y'all think? How should I handle these folks tellin' me to go easy on 'em?'
12.10: His boys hyped him up: 'Man, tell 'em, "If you thought my dad was tough, you ain't seen nothin' yet!"'
12.11: 'My pops used whips, but I'ma hit y'all with scorpions!'
12.12: Three days later, Jeroboam and all the people came back, just like the king told them.
12.13: But Rehoboam ignored the elders' advice and went with the foolishness his boys told him.
12.14: He doubled down: 'My dad was strict? I'ma be stricter. He whipped y'all? I'ma hit harder.'
12.15: Rehoboam ain't realize—this was God's plan all along, just like He told Jeroboam through the prophet Ahijah.
12.16: When the people heard this, they were DONE. They snapped back: 'Man, forget David's family! We got no part in his house! Y'all from Judah? Handle your own business! We out!'
12.17: From that day, Rehoboam only ruled the tribe of Judah—Israel walked away from the dynasty of David.
12.18: Then Rehoboam sent Adoram, his tax collector, to calm things down. Big mistake. The people straight up stoned him to death.
12.19: Rehoboam barely made it out alive—he had to hop in his chariot and run back to Jerusalem.
12.20: Soon as they heard Jeroboam was back, the people made him king over all Israel. Only Judah stayed loyal to Rehoboam.
12.21: Rehoboam wasn't about to let that slide. He gathered 180,000 warriors from Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel and take the kingdom back.
12.22: But then, God sent a message to a prophet named Shemaiah.
12.23: God said, 'Go tell Rehoboam, king of Judah, and all these folks with him…'
12.24: 'STOP. Don't fight your own people. This split is My doing.'
12.25: And they actually listened—Rehoboam and his army went home.
12.26: Meanwhile, Jeroboam was lowkey nervous. He thought, 'Man, if the people keep goin' to Jerusalem to worship at the Lord's temple…'
12.27: 'They gon' start feelin' loyal to Rehoboam again—and they might even kill me to go back to him!'
12.28: So instead of trusting God, he came up with his own plan—he made two golden calves. Then he told the people: 'Y'all don't need to go all the way to Jerusalem! Look, here are your gods that brought y'all outta Egypt!'
12.29: He put one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, so the people wouldn't go back to Judah to worship.
12.30: Big mistake—this turned into a huge sin 'cause now people were worshiping these fake gods all over the place.
12.31: Jeroboam even made random folks priests—not from the tribe of Levi, like God commanded.
12.32: Then he set up a fake holiday in the eighth month, kinda like the Feast of Tabernacles in Judah.
12.33: On that day, he personally offered sacrifices at Bethel to the golden calf. He made priests and burned incense at the altar.

13.1: One day, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel, just as Jeroboam was standing by the altar, burning incense.
13.2: The prophet shouted, 'Hey, altar! Listen up! The Lord says, a king named Josiah will be born in David's house. One day, he's gonna sacrifice all these fake priests y'all got burnin' incense on you, and human bones gon' be burned here!'
13.3: And to prove it, here's a sign: This altar gon' crack wide open, and the ashes will spill out!'
13.4: Jeroboam was HEATED. He pointed at the prophet and yelled, 'Somebody arrest this man!' But as soon as he stretched his hand out, it shriveled up!
13.5: Then BOOM—the altar split in two, just like the prophet said! Ashes went everywhere.
13.6: Jeroboam panicked. He begged the prophet, 'Please, pray to your God for me! Ask Him to heal my hand!'
13.7: So the prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed instantly.
13.8: The king was shook. He told the prophet, 'Come eat with me—I'll hook you up with a reward.'
13.9: But the man of God said, 'Nah, even if you gave me half your palace, I wouldn't go with you. The Lord told me, don't eat, don't drink, and don't go back the way I came.'
13.10: So he left Bethel and took a different route home.
13.11: Meanwhile, an old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and told him everything that just went down.
13.12: He asked them, 'Which way did he go?' They told him the direction.
13.13: The old prophet said, 'Saddle my donkey.' So they did, and he took off after the man of God.
13.14: He caught up with him, chillin' under an oak tree. He asked, 'You the man of God from Judah?'
13.16: The old man invited him, 'Come eat at my house.'
13.17: The prophet replied, 'Can't do it. The Lord said no food, no drink, and don't go back the same way.'
13.18: But the old man LIED. He said, 'I'm a prophet too, and an angel told me it's fine.'
13.19: So the man of God went with him and ate at his house.
13.20: While they were eatin', the Lord spoke through the old prophet and called the man of God out.
13.21: 'The Lord says, you disobeyed! You ate and drank in the place I told you NOT to!
13.22: So now, you won't even be buried in your family's tomb.'
13.23: After they finished eating, the old prophet saddled up the man of God's donkey.
13.24: But on his way home, a lion jumped out and killed him! His body lay on the road, with the lion and the donkey just standing there.
13.25: Some travelers saw the scene and ran back to town to spread the news.
13.26: The old prophet heard about it and said, 'Welp, that's the man of God. He disobeyed the Lord, and the lion took him out—just like God said.'
13.27: He told his sons, 'Saddle up my donkey.'
13.28: He found the prophet's body on the road. The donkey was still standing there. The lion hadn't eaten the body or killed the donkey.
13.29: He picked up the prophet's body, put it on his donkey, and brought it back home.
13.30: Then he buried him and mourned, saying, 'Man, my brother!'
13.31: Later, he told his sons, 'When I die, bury me next to him.'
13.32: 'Everything he said about the altar in Bethel and the high places WILL come true.'
13.33: Even after all that, Jeroboam STILL didn't turn from his evil ways.
13.34: He kept making random people priests, even though they weren't Levites. If you wanted to be a priest, he'd let you.
13.35: That one decision became his downfall and led to the destruction of his whole dynasty.

14.1: Around that time, Jeroboam's son Abijah got real sick.
14.2: Jeroboam told his wife, 'Look, I need you to go see the prophet Ahijah in Shiloh. But listen, don't let nobody know you my wife. He's the same prophet who told me I'd be king.
14.3: Take ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and honey, and go ask him what's gonna happen to our son.
14.4: So Jeroboam's wife put on a disguise and went to Ahijah's house. But the prophet was already blind from old age.
14.5: But God already told Ahijah, 'Jeroboam's wife is coming, pretending to be somebody else. Here's what you gon' tell her when she asks about her son.'
14.6: As soon as she walked in, Ahijah said, 'Come on in, Jeroboam's wife! Why you tryna pretend? I got bad news for you.
14.7: Go tell Jeroboam, 'The Lord says: I made you king, lifted you up from the people.'
14.8: I took the kingdom from David's family and gave it to you, but you ain't been nothing like David. He followed Me with all his heart, but you? You out here wildin'!
14.9: You did more evil than anybody before you! You made fake gods, idols, and straight up disrespected Me.
14.10: So guess what? Your whole house is getting wiped out. Every last male in Israel who's tied to you is done.
14.11: If they die in the city, dogs will eat 'em. If they die in the field, birds gon' pick 'em clean. The Lord said it, and it's done.'
14.12: Now, go home. Soon as you step foot in the city, your son is gonna die.
14.13: And all Israel will mourn for him, but he's the only one in your family who'll get a proper burial. He's the only one who had any good in him.
14.14: The Lord already picked a new king who's gonna wipe out your whole bloodline.
14.15: Israel gon' be shaken like a reed in the water. God's gon' kick them out of this land and scatter them beyond the river. Why? Because of all these fake gods they keep worshiping.
14.16: And all this is happening because you, Jeroboam, led them into sin.'
14.17: Jeroboam's wife went home to Tirzah, and as soon as she stepped over the threshold, the boy died.
14.18: All of Israel mourned and buried him, just like the prophet said.
14.19: The rest of Jeroboam's story—his wars, his reign—it's all written down in the royal records.
14.20: Jeroboam ruled for 22 years. Then he died, and his son Nadab took the throne.
14.21: Meanwhile, Solomon's son Rehoboam was king over Judah. He was 41 years old when he took the throne and ruled for 17 years in Jerusalem.
14.22: But Judah? They did evil in the Lord's sight. Way worse than their ancestors.
14.23: They built altars, sacred pillars, and idols on every high hill and under every green tree.
14.24: There were male cult prostitutes in the land, and Judah was out here doing the same nasty stuff as the nations God kicked out before them.
14.25: In Rehoboam's 5th year as king, Egypt's king Shishak attacked Jerusalem.
14.26: He raided the temple and the royal palace, taking all the treasures—including Solomon's gold shields!
14.27: So Rehoboam had to replace them with bronze shields. Every time he went to the temple, the guards had to carry them, then lock them back up.
14.28: Ain't no gold left. Just bronze.
14.29: The rest of Rehoboam's rule? It's all in the royal records.
14.30: There was constant beef between him and Jeroboam the whole time.
14.31: Then Rehoboam died, got buried in the City of David, and his son Abijam took over.

15.1: In the 18th year of King Jeroboam's reign, Abijam became king over Judah.
15.2: He ruled for three years in Jerusalem. His mama's name was Maachah, granddaughter of Abishalom.
15.3: But he wasn't loyal to God. Just like his daddy before him, he was out here wildin'.
15.4: But for David's sake, the Lord still kept Judah going and let Abijam's son take the throne after him.
15.5: See, David did right by God his whole life—except that one time with Uriah the Hittite.
15.6: And trust, the beef between Rehoboam and Jeroboam stayed strong all their days.
15.7: Everything else Abijam did? It's all in the royal records. And yeah, he stayed at war with Jeroboam too.
15.8: Then Abijam died, got buried in the City of David, and his son Asa took the throne.
15.9: In Jeroboam's 20th year as king, Asa became king over Judah.
15.10: He ruled for 41 years in Jerusalem. His grandma was Maachah, granddaughter of Abishalom.
15.11: But Asa was different—he did right in the eyes of the Lord, just like his ancestor David.
15.12: He kicked out the male shrine prostitutes and tore down all the idols his ancestors made.
15.13: Even his own grandma, Maachah, had to go! She had an obscene Asherah idol, so Asa snatched it down and burned it by the Brook Kidron.
15.14: Now, he didn't take down every high place, but Asa's heart stayed loyal to the Lord his whole life.
15.15: He also brought back the silver, gold, and sacred items into the house of the Lord.
15.16: Asa and Baasha, king of Israel, were at war the whole time.
15.17: Baasha set up shop in Ramah, blocking trade so nobody could come in or out of Judah.
15.18: So Asa took all the gold and silver left in the Lord's temple and his palace and sent it to Ben-Hadad, king of Syria.
15.19: He told Ben-Hadad, 'Yo, let's make a treaty like our daddies did. I'm sending you a little gift—now break your treaty with Baasha so he'll back off.'
15.20: Ben-Hadad was with it. He sent his army to attack Israel, hitting Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maachah, Chinneroth, and all of Naphtali.
15.21: When Baasha got the news, he stopped building Ramah and dipped back to Tirzah.
15.22: Then Asa told all of Judah, 'Go grab the stones and timber from Ramah!' And with those supplies, he built up Geba and Mizpah.
15.23: Everything else Asa did—his cities, his power—it's all in the royal records. But in his old age, his feet got messed up.
15.24: Then Asa died, got buried in the City of David, and his son Jehoshaphat took over.
15.25: Meanwhile, Jeroboam's son Nadab became king over Israel in Asa's 2nd year. He ruled for only 2 years.
15.26: But just like his daddy, he did evil in the Lord's sight and led Israel into sin.
15.27: Then Baasha, son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, plotted against him. He killed Nadab at Gibbethon, while Nadab was trying to siege the Philistines.
15.28: Baasha took him out in Asa's 3rd year and claimed the throne.
15.29: And just like God warned, Baasha wiped out Jeroboam's whole bloodline. Not one of his descendants survived.
15.30: This all happened because Jeroboam made Israel sin, provoking the Lord's anger.
15.31: Everything else Nadab did? It's in the royal records.
15.32: And yeah, the war between Asa and Baasha kept going strong.
15.33: In Asa's 3rd year, Baasha became king over Israel and ruled from Tirzah for 24 years.
15.34: But he wasn't any better. He did evil and followed in Jeroboam's footsteps, making Israel sin.

16.1: Then the word of the Lord came to Jehu son of Hanani, speaking against Baasha.
16.2: God said, 'I pulled you up out the dust and made you king over My people, but you went and did the same evil Jeroboam did. You led My people into sin and got Me mad.'
16.3: 'So now, I'm wiping out your whole family. You ain't gonna have no legacy—your house gonna be like Jeroboam's.
16.4: If you die in the city, dogs gonna eat you. If you die in the field, birds gonna eat you.
16.5: The rest of Baasha's life? His battles? His power? It's all in the royal records.
16.6: Baasha died, got buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah took over.
16.7: And the Lord made sure Baasha's house got wiped out because of all the evil he did. He provoked God just like Jeroboam.
16.8: In Asa's 26th year as king, Elah became king of Israel and ruled for two years in Tirzah.
16.9: But his own officer, Zimri, who was over half his chariots, plotted against him. Elah was getting wasted in his steward's house in Tirzah.
16.10: Zimri walked in, killed him, and took the throne in Asa's 27th year.
16.11: As soon as Zimri sat on the throne, he killed every last male in Baasha's house. No family, no friends—nobody survived.
16.12: And just like God said through Jehu, Baasha's house was wiped off the map.
16.13: All because Baasha and Elah led Israel into sin, making God furious with their idols.
16.14: Everything else Elah did? It's in the royal records.
16.15: In Asa's 27th year, Zimri ruled Israel for just seven days. Meanwhile, the army was out fighting the Philistines.
16.16: When the soldiers heard that Zimri killed the king, they made their commander, Omri, the new king.
16.17: Omri and the army marched to Tirzah, surrounded it, and prepared to attack.
16.18: When Zimri saw he was done for, he set the king's house on fire—while he was inside. He died in the flames.
16.19: This happened because Zimri followed Jeroboam's sins, making Israel turn against God.
16.20: Everything else Zimri did? It's in the royal records.
16.21: But Israel was divided—half wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, and half followed Omri.
16.22: Omri's side won the battle, Tibni died, and Omri ruled Israel.
16.23: In Asa's 31st year, Omri became king over Israel and ruled 12 years. Six of those years he ruled from Tirzah.
16.24: Then he bought a hill from a man named Shemer for two talents of silver. He built a new city there and named it Samaria.
16.25: Omri was even worse than all the kings before him.
16.26: He did exactly what Jeroboam did, leading Israel into sin and making God furious.
16.27: Everything else Omri did? It's in the royal records.
16.28: Then Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab took the throne.
16.29: In Asa's 38th year, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel. He ruled for 22 years in Samaria.
16.30: Ahab was the most wicked king Israel ever had—even worse than those before him.
16.31: Like it wasn't already bad enough, he married Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Then he started worshipping Baal.
16.32: He built a temple for Baal in Samaria and set up an altar inside it.
16.33: He also made Asherah poles. Ahab did more to anger God than any king before him.
16.34: And in his time, Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho, fulfilling the curse Joshua spoke. He laid its foundation with his firstborn Abiram and set up its gates with his youngest Segub.

17.1: Elijah the Tishbite, from Gilead, told Ahab, 'As sure as God lives, there ain't gonna be no dew or rain for years—unless I say so.'
17.2: Then the Lord spoke to Elijah,
17.3: 'You gotta get outta here. Head east and hide by the Brook Cherith, near the Jordan.'
17.4: 'Drink from the brook. And don't trip, I already told the ravens to bring you food.'
17.5: So Elijah listened to God. He went to the Brook Cherith and stayed there.
17.6: The ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.
17.7: But after a while, the brook dried up—since there was no rain.
17.9: 'Get up and go to Zarephath in Sidon. A widow there will take care of you.'
17.10: Elijah arrived at the city gates and saw a widow gathering sticks. He asked her, 'Could you bring me some water?'
17.11: As she was going to get it, he called out again, 'And bring me a little bread too!'
17.12: She said, 'Sir, I barely got anything left. Just a handful of flour and a little oil. I was about to make a last meal for me and my son, then die.'
17.13: Elijah told her, 'Don't be scared. Just do what you said, but make me a small cake first. Then, you and your son can eat after.'
17.14: 'The Lord said your flour and oil ain't gonna run out until He sends rain again!'
17.15: So she did what Elijah said. She, Elijah, and her son had food for days.
17.16: Her flour never ran out, and her oil never dried up—just like God said through Elijah.
17.17: But later, her son got real sick. He got so bad, he stopped breathing.
17.18: The woman told Elijah, 'What you got against me, man of God? You came here just to remind me of my sins and let my son die?!'
17.19: Elijah said, 'Give me your son.' He took him upstairs, laid him on the bed.
17.20: Elijah cried out, 'Lord, really? You brought me here just to take this widow's son?!'
17.21: Then Elijah stretched out on the boy three times and prayed, 'Lord, let this child's soul come back!'
17.22: God heard Elijah, and the boy came back to life.
17.23: Elijah carried the boy downstairs, gave him back to his mother, and said, 'Look, your son is alive!'
17.24: The woman said, 'Now I know for sure you're a man of God, and everything you say from God is the truth!'

18.1: After a long time, God told Elijah, 'Go see Ahab—I'm bout to send rain again.'
18.2: So Elijah went to find Ahab. Meanwhile, Samaria was goin' through a serious famine.
18.3: Now Ahab had a servant named Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. (And Obadiah feared the Lord big time.
18.4: While Jezebel was out here killing God's prophets, Obadiah hid 100 of them in caves—50 in each cave—and made sure they had bread and water.
18.5: Ahab told Obadiah, 'Go check all the springs and brooks. Maybe we can find enough grass to keep our horses and mules alive.'
18.6: So they split up—Ahab went one way, and Obadiah went another.
18.7: As Obadiah was out searchin', Elijah ran into him. Obadiah saw him and was like, 'Wait…is that really you, Elijah?!'
18.8: Elijah said, 'Yeah, it's me. Go tell Ahab I'm here.'
18.9: Obadiah was like, 'Man, what did I do wrong that you tryna get me killed?!'
18.10: 'Ahab been searchin' for you everywhere! Every kingdom, every nation—and made 'em swear they hadn't seen you.
18.11: And now you want me to just roll up to him and say, "Elijah's here"?!'
18.12: 'As soon as I leave, God gon' snatch you away somewhere. Then when Ahab don't find you, he gon' kill me!'
18.13: 'Ain't you heard what I did? I saved 100 of the Lord's prophets! Hid 'em in caves! Fed them bread and water!'
18.14: 'And now you tellin' me to tell Ahab, "Elijah's here"? He gon' kill me!'
18.15: Elijah said, 'Look, God is my witness—I'ma see Ahab TODAY.'
18.16: So Obadiah went to tell Ahab, and Ahab came out to meet Elijah.
18.17: When Ahab saw him, he said, 'Oh, look who it is—the man causing all this trouble in Israel!'
18.18: Elijah shot back, 'Nah, that's YOU & YOUR FAMILY! Y'all the ones turned away from God and started worshiping Baal!
18.19: 'So here's what you do—bring ALL Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. And bring 450 prophets of Baal & 400 prophets of Asherah—you know, the ones Jezebel feeds at her table.'
18.20: So Ahab sent word, and all of Israel and the false prophets came to Mount Carmel.
18.21: Elijah stepped up and said, 'How long y'all gon' be stuck between two choices? If the Lord is God, follow Him. If Baal is God, follow him.'
18.22: Elijah said, 'Look, I'm the last prophet left of the Lord. But Baal got 450 prophets.
18.23: 'So let's do this—bring two bulls. Let them choose one, cut it up, put it on wood—but don't set no fire. I'ma do the same thing.
18.24: 'Then y'all call on Baal, and I'ma call on the Lord. The God who sends fire—THAT'S the real God.'
18.25: Elijah told Baal's prophets, 'Y'all go first—there's a lot of y'all. Call on Baal, but don't set no fire.'
18.26: So they called on Baal from morning 'til noon. 'O Baal, hear us!' But no answer. They started jumping around the altar.
18.27: Around noon, Elijah started clownin' them. 'Maybe he's busy? Maybe he's sleep? Maybe he on vacation? Y'all better yell louder!'
18.28: So they started shouting & cutting themselves with knives, like they usually did. Blood was everywhere.
18.29: They kept this up until evening. But still no voice, no answer—nothing.
18.30: Then Elijah said, 'Y'all come over here.' So the people came near, and he rebuilt the Lord's altar that had been torn down.
18.31: He took 12 stones (one for each tribe of Israel).
18.32: With those stones, he built an altar for the Lord, dug a trench around it.
18.33: He put wood down, cut up the bull, laid it out. Then he said, 'Fill four big jugs of water & pour it all over the sacrifice.'
18.34: Then he said, 'Do it again.' They did. Then he said, 'One more time.' And they poured water a third time.
18.35: The water ran everywhere—even filled the trench.
18.36: At evening time, Elijah prayed, 'Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, & Israel, show these people today that YOU are God!'
18.37: 'Let them see Your power & turn back to You!'
18.38: Then—BOOM! Fire fell from heaven—burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the dust, AND dried up all the water.
18.39: The people fell on their faces and cried out, 'The Lord is God! The Lord is God!'
18.40: Then Elijah said, 'Grab every prophet of Baal! Don't let a single one escape!' So they seized them, and Elijah executed them at the Brook Kishon.
18.41: Elijah told Ahab, 'Go eat & drink—rain is coming!'
18.42: Ahab went up to eat, but Elijah went to the top of Mount Carmel, bowed down, and prayed.
18.43: He told his servant, 'Go look toward the sea.' The servant came back: 'I don't see nothin'.'
18.44: Finally, the servant said, 'I see a tiny cloud, the size of a man's hand.'
18.45: The sky got dark with clouds, the wind picked up, and a heavy rain started pouring. Ahab rode off to Jezreel.
18.46: Then the Spirit of the Lord came upon Elijah, and he outran Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel!

19.1: Ahab went and told Jezebel everything Elijah had done—including how he had killed all the prophets of Baal.
19.2: Jezebel sent a message to Elijah: 'By this time tomorrow, I swear I'ma do you just like you did them prophets. If I don't, may the gods punish me even worse!'
19.3: Elijah saw that and was like, 'I gotta get outta here.' He ran for his life, went all the way to Beersheba in Judah, and left his servant there.
19.4: Then Elijah went even further into the wilderness, sat under a tree, and prayed, 'Lord, just take me now. I can't do this no more.'
19.5: He lay down and fell asleep under the tree. But then an angel tapped him and said, 'Get up and eat.'
19.6: Elijah woke up, looked around, and saw a cake baked on hot coals & a jar of water. So he ate, drank, and went back to sleep.
19.7: The angel came back, tapped him again, and said, 'Get up and eat—this journey you on is too much for you.'
19.8: So Elijah got up, ate, drank, and that meal kept him going for 40 days & 40 nights until he got to Mount Horeb, the mountain of God.
19.9: Elijah went into a cave and stayed the night. Then God spoke: 'Elijah, what you doing here?'
19.10: Elijah said, 'Lord, I been working hard for You! But Israel? They broke Your covenant, tore down Your altars, and killed all Your prophets. I'm the last one left—and now they tryna kill me too!'
19.11: God said, 'Go stand on the mountain. I'm about to pass by.' Then came a powerful wind—tearing up mountains & breaking rocks! But God wasn't in the wind. Then an earthquake! But God wasn't in the earthquake.
19.12: Then a fire! But God wasn't in the fire. Then... a small whisper. Elijah heard that whisper, wrapped his cloak around his face, and stepped out the cave.
19.13: Then the voice asked again, 'Elijah, what are you doing here?'
19.14: Elijah repeated, 'Lord, I been workin' hard for You. But Israel betrayed You! They tore down Your altars, killed Your prophets, and now they tryna kill me too.'
19.15: The Lord said, 'Go back the way you came, but this time, head to the Wilderness of Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as king of Syria.'
19.16: 'Then, anoint Jehu as king of Israel.'
19.17: 'Whoever escapes Hazael's sword, Jehu gon' kill. Whoever escapes Jehu's sword, Elisha gon' handle them.'
19.18: 'But listen, you ain't the only one left. I got 7,000 people in Israel who ain't bowed to Baal or kissed him.'
19.19: So Elijah left and found Elisha, who was plowing with 12 yoke of oxen. Elijah walked by him and threw his mantle (cloak) over him.
19.20: Elisha ran after Elijah and said, 'Let me go kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll follow you.' Elijah said, 'Go ahead, but remember what just happened here.'
19.21: So Elisha went back, took his oxen, sacrificed them, and cooked them. He gave the food to the people, then left to follow Elijah and became his servant.

20.1: Ben-Hadad, king of Syria, rolled up with 32 other kings, horses, and chariots. He laid siege to Samaria and declared war on it.
20.2: He sent messengers to Ahab, king of Israel, saying, 'This is what Ben-Hadad says—'
20.3: 'Run me your silver and gold. Your finest wives & kids belong to me now.'
20.4: Ahab responded, 'You got it, my lord and king. Everything I have is yours.'
20.5: But the messengers came back, saying, 'Ben-Hadad says, "Nah, I ain't just talking about your silver & gold. Tomorrow, my men are coming to your palace to take anything they like."'
20.6: 'And they'll search your officials' houses too. If it's valuable, it's ours.'
20.7: Ahab called a meeting with his elders and said, 'Y'all see what's happening? This man wants war! He already took my silver, my gold, my wives, my kids—now he wants everything.'
20.8: The elders & people said, 'Don't listen to him! Don't agree!'
20.9: So Ahab sent messengers back, saying, 'I agreed to your first demand, but this second one? Nope.'
20.10: Ben-Hadad fired back, 'By the gods, I swear there won't be enough dust left of Samaria for my soldiers to pick up in their hands.'
20.11: Ahab hit him with a cold clapback: 'Don't talk like you already won. The man putting his armor on shouldn't brag like the one taking it off after battle.'
20.12: Ben-Hadad was drunk when he got the message. He snapped, 'Get ready! Attack the city!'
20.13: A prophet rolled up to Ahab and said, 'Look at this army. God says, "I'ma give you this win today so you KNOW I'm the Lord."'
20.14: Ahab asked, 'Who's gonna fight this battle?' The prophet said, 'Your young officers.' Ahab asked, 'Who's leading?' The prophet said, 'You.'
20.15: So Ahab rounded up 232 young officers. Then he called the rest of Israel—7,000 soldiers.
20.16: They attacked at noon. Meanwhile, Ben-Hadad and his 32 allied kings? Drunk outta their minds in their tent.
20.17: The young officers marched out first. Ben-Hadad's scouts ran back saying, 'Uh, some men are coming from Samaria!'
20.18: Ben-Hadad, still tipsy, said, 'If they coming in peace, take them alive. If they coming for war, take them alive.'
20.19: The officers charged. The Israelites followed.
20.20: Each soldier handled his opponent, and Syria's army fled. Ben-Hadad hopped on a horse and dipped!
20.21: Ahab came through, wrecked their chariots, killed the cavalry, and left Syria in ruins.
20.22: A prophet told Ahab, 'Get ready. Ben-Hadad will be back next spring.'
20.23: Meanwhile, Syria's officials told Ben-Hadad, 'Listen, Israel's God is a "mountain god." That's why we lost. If we fight on flatland, we'll win.'
20.24: 'Swap out the kings for real commanders and build a bigger army. Fight in the plains next time.'
20.26: The next spring, Syria pulled up to Aphek ready for round 2.
20.27: Israel came too, but they looked like tiny flocks compared to Syria's huge army.
20.28: A man of God came to Ahab and said, 'Because Syria disrespected God, saying He only runs the mountains, He's about to let you WIN so you know who He is.'
20.29: Both armies camped for 7 days. On day 7? They clashed.
20.30: Israel killed 100,000 soldiers in ONE day. The rest ran to Aphek, but then? A WALL collapsed and killed 27,000 more!
20.31: Ben-Hadad's men told him, 'Israelite kings show mercy. Wear sackcloth & ropes. Beg Ahab for your life.'
20.32: They went to Ahab and said, 'Your servant Ben-Hadad is asking to live.' Ahab said, 'Wait… he's alive? He my brother then.'
20.33: The men saw Ahab was open to peace, so they pushed harder: 'Yes, Ben-Hadad is your brother!'
20.34: Ben-Hadad told Ahab, 'I'ma give back the cities my dad took from your dad. You can set up markets in Damascus, just like my dad did in Samaria.' Ahab said, 'Bet. Let's make a treaty.' Then he let him go.
20.35: One of God's prophets told a man, 'Hit me!' But the man refused.
20.36: So the prophet said, 'Because you ain't listen, a lion finna eat you.' Sure enough? Dude got eaten by a lion.
20.37: The prophet found another man and said, 'Hit me!' So the man hit him hard.
20.38: The prophet then disguised himself, covering his wounds with a bandage.
20.39: As Ahab passed by, the prophet yelled, 'King! I was in battle, and a soldier brought me a prisoner, telling me to guard him. If he escaped, I'd owe a fine or my life! But I got distracted… and he ran away!'
20.40: Ahab told him, 'Then that's your problem. You just judged yourself.'
20.41: Then the prophet pulled off his disguise and Ahab realized he was a prophet.
20.42: The prophet said, 'God says—since you let go the man I sentenced to die, YOUR life will go for HIS. Your people will pay for it too.'

21.1: After all that went down, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard right next to Ahab's palace in Jezreel.
21.2: Ahab told Naboth, 'Lemme buy your vineyard. I wanna make it a garden since it's close to my palace. I'll give you a better vineyard for it, or cash if you prefer.'
21.3: But Naboth said, 'God forbid I sell my family's land!'
21.4: Ahab went home mad & salty over Naboth's refusal. He threw himself on the bed, turned his face to the wall, and refused to eat.
21.5: Jezebel came in like, 'What's wrong with you? Why you pouting like this?'
21.6: Ahab told her, 'I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard, even offered to trade him a better one. But he said no.'
21.7: Jezebel rolled her eyes and said, 'Boy, you the king! Get up, eat some food, stop sulking. I'll get you that vineyard.'
21.8: She wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them, and sent them to the city leaders.
21.9: The letter said: 'Call a fast, put Naboth at the head of the people—'
21.10: 'Then seat two liars next to him who'll say, "Naboth cursed God & the king!" Then take him outside and stone him to death.'
21.11: The city elders did exactly as Jezebel ordered.
21.12: They called a fast and sat Naboth up front.
21.13: Then two fake witnesses came and accused him of cursing God & the king. So they took him outside and stoned him to death.
21.14: They sent word to Jezebel: 'Naboth is dead.'
21.15: Jezebel told Ahab, 'Get up! Take Naboth's vineyard. He dead now.'
21.16: Ahab, all happy again, went straight down to claim the vineyard.
21.17: God told Elijah: 'Go down to meet Ahab. He's in Naboth's vineyard, taking it for himself.'
21.18: 'Tell him: "So you murdered a man & stole his land too?"'
21.19: 'Then say: "God says—where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they gon' lick up yours too."'
21.20: Ahab saw Elijah and said, 'Oh great, my enemy found me.' Elijah said, 'Yeah, I found you. Cuz you sold yourself to evil.'
21.21: 'God says—I'm wiping out your family. No sons, no legacy.'
21.22: 'I'ma make your house like Jeroboam's and Baasha's, cuz you made Israel sin.'
21.23: 'Oh, and Jezebel? She gon' get eaten by dogs in Jezreel.'
21.24: 'Anybody from Ahab's family that dies in the city? Dogs eating them. Anybody that dies in the fields? Birds eating them.'
21.25: Ahab was the worst king Israel ever had. Jezebel pushed him to do evil.
21.26: He followed false gods, just like the Amorites God had wiped out.
21.27: When Ahab heard this, he tore his clothes, wore sackcloth, fasted, and humbled himself.
21.28: God told Elijah, 'See how Ahab humbled himself? I won't bring disaster in his lifetime.'
21.29: 'But his son? That's when it's all coming down.'

22.1: Ain't been no war between Syria and Israel for three years.
22.2: But in the third year, Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, went to visit the king of Israel.
22.3: The king of Israel told his crew, "Y'all know Ramoth-Gilead belong to us, right? But we just sittin' here while Syria holdin' it down?"
22.4: So he asked Jehoshaphat, "You ridin' with me to take it back?" Jehoshaphat said, "You already know—me, my people, my horses, all of us, we wit' you."
22.5: But then Jehoshaphat was like, "Hold up, we need to ask the Lord about this first."
22.6: So the king of Israel called together 400 prophets and asked them, "Should I go to war for Ramoth-Gilead, or nah?" They all said, "Go ahead! The Lord gon' hand it to you!"
22.7: But Jehoshaphat wasn't feelin' that, so he asked, "Ain't there at least one real prophet of the Lord we can check with?"
22.8: The king of Israel said, "Yeah, there's Micaiah, son of Imlah. But I don't like him—he never got nothin' good to say about me, always talkin' negative." Jehoshaphat said, "Man, don't talk like that!"
22.9: So the king called for one of his men and said, "Go get Micaiah, now!"
22.10: Meanwhile, both kings—Israel and Judah—were sittin' on their thrones, posted up at the city gate, watchin' as all the prophets kept prophesyin'.
22.11: One prophet, Zedekiah, made some iron horns and said, "The Lord says you gon' charge through the Syrians like this and wipe 'em out!"
22.12: All the prophets kept sayin' the same thing, "Go up to Ramoth-Gilead! The Lord gon' give you the win!"
22.13: The messenger who went to get Micaiah told him, "Look, everybody else already sayin' good things to the king. Just say what they say, aight?"
